what_they_do.value: Attio is the platform that builds pipeline, advances deals, and grows accounts around the clock.

priorities.priority: Build the architecture for agentic revenue: a hybrid platform designed for people and AI agents.
priorities.evidence: Attio says it is introducing a new shape of software and is launching SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale, and Activities in beta to help teams scale revenue motions.

priorities.priority: Make Workflows the operating layer for AI-assisted revenue orchestration.
priorities.evidence: Attio describes Workflows as its engine for orchestrating AI agents across every account and signal, covering prospecting, lead triage, briefings, follow-up, stalled-deal revival, and signal-based outreach.

priorities.priority: Scale the data and developer platform so CRM data is queryable, connected, extensible, and usable by agents.
priorities.evidence: The architecture announcement highlights SQL access, a live Postgres-compatible data connector, support for hundreds of millions of records, and structured Activities; the Product Lead role also calls for scalable foundations, AI capabilities, APIs, schemas, and platform architecture.

priorities.priority: Invest in product and engineering talent and ship rapidly while expanding the platform globally.
priorities.evidence: Attio's funding announcement says it is scaling engineering, expanding globally, and accelerating AI-primitives development; its current Product Lead posting says the team ships constantly and is hiring people to extend AI capabilities and guide the next generation of the platform.

challenges.challenge: Turning AI-agent capability into reliable, governed work at scale.
challenges.evidence: Attio explicitly frames the problem as software not being built for agents and emphasizes permissions, inspectable agent actions, reliability, and control; the Product Lead role calls out trade-offs among speed, safety, usability, performance, and architectural scale.

challenges.challenge: Competing against legacy CRM assumptions and a fragmented GTM-tool ecosystem.
challenges.evidence: Attio says legacy CRMs assume manual inputs, rigid workflows, and human-only operators, while core GTM capabilities have historically been spread across thousands of point tools requiring costly integrations.

challenges.challenge: Maintaining product simplicity and customer experience as the product surface and technical complexity expand.
challenges.evidence: The Product Lead brief says Attio needs people comfortable with complex data models, edge cases, schemas, API design, performance, safety, usability, and building foundations that scale while preserving a best-in-class customer experience.

recent_changes.headline: Workflow history and agent log
recent_changes.summary: Attio added visibility into every workflow run and agent step, including tools called, records changed, and credits used.

recent_changes.headline: New workflow blocks and app updates
recent_changes.summary: Attio added call-recording and meeting-linking workflow blocks, plus Resend and ClickUp integrations; Aircall now writes AI call summaries into notes.

recent_changes.headline: New Workflows apps, blocks, and developer-platform updates
recent_changes.summary: Attio added Google Sheets, Asana, and Hunter workflow apps, expanded workflow controls, and shipped new API/MCP capabilities plus a stable App SDK 1.0.0.

recent_changes.headline: Formula attributes, new workflow blocks, and more Ask Attio models
recent_changes.summary: The July changelog records new formula attributes, workflow blocks, mobile performance improvements, and additional models in Ask Attio.

key_people.name: Nicolas Sharp
key_people.title: CEO & Co-founder
key_people.recent: In announcing the Inconvo team joining Attio, Sharp said the company is building a CRM with first-class agentic access across every surface and that the new engineers fit Attio's builder philosophy.

key_people.name: Eoghan Mulcahy
key_people.title: Co-founder of Inconvo; joining Attio Engineering
key_people.recent: He joined Attio's Engineering team and said he was excited to help shape how AI becomes part of the CRM experience.

key_people.name: Liam Mulcahy
key_people.title: Co-founder of Inconvo; joining Attio Engineering
key_people.recent: He joined Attio's Engineering team and highlighted the combination of technical depth and care for users that attracted him to the company.

key_people.name: Michael McBride
key_people.title: GV board member
key_people.recent: He joined Attio's board as part of the Series B; Attio cited his experience scaling revenue more than 100x through GitLab's IPO and beyond.

talking_points: As Workflows expands across every account and signal, where does Attio most need stronger reliability, governance, or observability?
How are customers prioritizing the new SQL, Data Connectors, Activities, and App SDK capabilities—and which integrations or data sources are hardest to operationalize?
As Attio scales engineering and global go-to-market, how is the team balancing rapid AI shipping with simplicity, safety, and a best-in-class customer experience?
